title: Make content the documented proof of what shipped, fix three pointers to a renamed rule, and check for a prior measurement before calling one unverified

history.detail:
PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 47, round 1. Audited commit 8ff3988 (on 20cb32c, the sprint start). The sprint file was read fresh at HEAD and is unchanged since 20cb32c. Verdict: PASS.

1. Req 1 / 1a / 1b: liveqa.md carries a Provenance section making content comparison the standing check, with gitHead demoted to corroboration and the asymmetry stated (metadata attests what git said at one instant; content proves what the tarball is), and both questions named — content comparison cannot catch a right-content/wrong-commit publish, gitHead cannot catch content drift.
 - 1a's real risk was weakening Pipeman's publish-time stop condition. It is untouched: .claude/agents/pipeman.md has a zero-line diff across this whole sprint. The demotion is confined to LiveQA's side, exactly as required.
2. Req 1c: the script exists, is distinct from verify-tarball.sh (that one packs and checks a LOCAL pack; this one downloads a PUBLISHED release), and liveqa.md references it. I ran it myself against real releases rather than trusting the handoff:
 - 0.2.23 against its own audited commit 4602108: recomputes the tarball SHA-1 independently of npm's own check, then reports MATCHED 59, MISMATCHED 0, NOT-IN-COMMIT 0, PASSED, exit 0.
 - 0.2.23 against a deliberately WRONG commit (5d9f3c1): MATCHED 57, MISMATCHED 2 (CHANGELOG.md and pipeman.md, which are exactly the files that differ between those commits), FAILED, exit 1. So it detects real drift and names the files.
 - 0.2.22, the release with no gitHead at all: the script reports "gitHead ABSENT ... not a reason to fail this script" and still PASSES the content check on 59 files, exit 0. That is Req 1a's behaviour demonstrated end to end against the actual failed release, which is the best possible test case for it.
3. Req 2 / 2a: all three messages now name the rule by identity ("CLAUDE.md's publish-isolation rule: Pipeman publishes from a throwaway clone, never from this checkout"), and the anchor phrase exists in CLAUDE.md.
 - 2b: I ran my own sweep, and then falsified it, which matters more than the sweep itself. My first pattern returned nothing — but it also returned nothing when run against the PRE-FIX commit, where the three known stale pointers demonstrably existed, so it was vacuous (the character class excluded the dot in "CLAUDE.md"). Corrected pattern, re-run: at 20cb32c it finds exactly the three known pointers (mc-commit.js:410, sprint_lifecycle.py:4139, gate-commit.js:237); at 8ff3988 the only remaining hits are the CHANGELOG describing the fix, the smoke test's own literal asserting the string is gone, and the sprint file quoting the defect. A wider scan of every "sprint N's own ..." reference in shipped files turned up nothing pointing at content that has moved.
4. Req 3 / 3a / 3b: master-controller.md gains step 11 naming all four places (sprint files including closed ones, docs/ findings, CHANGELOG, and annotated tags with the actual commands to read them), requiring a prior measurement to be cited with a statement of whether it still applies, and re-measurement rather than a never-measured flag when it is wrong. 3a states the cost concretely: sprint 46's 0.2.22 published with no gitHead, a FAIL round and a fix round, from a fact recorded twice twenty days earlier. 3b holds: sprint_lifecycle.py's only change in this sprint is comment/message text, no command gained a gate.
5. Req 5: I confirmed the new tests actually exercise a planted mismatch, per the acceptance criterion, and my first attempt at that control was invalid — worth recording, because an invalid negative control is how a vacuous test passes review. I first edited a line that turned out to be the MISMATCHED initializer, which the increments below simply overwrote; the suite passed and proved nothing. Breaking the real comparison branch instead (forcing the diff test to always report a match) makes the script wrongly report PASSED on the known-mismatch case, and the smoke suite then FAILS with "expected exit code 1 on a real content mismatch, got 0". So the coverage is genuine.
 - The smoke coverage runs against a throwaway sandbox with a faked npm binary, never this repository's real history or the live registry, which is the right isolation for a test that would otherwise depend on the network and on published state.
6. Req 4: package.json is 0.2.24 against published 0.2.23, with a CHANGELOG entry covering Reqs 1-3.
7. Both suites pass at 8ff3988 in a clean clone: node scripts/launcher_test.js ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0; bash scripts/smoke_test.sh ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0.

ON THE TWO STATED LIMITATIONS, both correctly disclosed and neither blocking:
 - No standing CI guard that pipeman.md's step 10.3 never changes. Correct that this is a one-time confirmation; I verified the zero-line diff myself this round, and a future sprint touching that file would be visible in its own diff.
 - The stale-pointer test is a regression test for this specific string, not a general staleness prover, and says so in its own comment. That is the honest scope, and the alternative (a general "is this reference still true" mechanism) is explicitly Out of Scope here.

FOR LIVEQA. The sprint's own criterion is the right one and it is the whole point of Req 1c: run scripts/verify-release-content.sh against the published 0.2.24 and the audited commit, and report the three counts. I have already demonstrated the script's three behaviours against real releases at build time, so a failure at gate time means something changed in the release, not that the script is unproven. Also confirm gitHead is present and correct for 0.2.24 (Pipeman's check is unchanged), and report the two as answering different questions rather than one standing in for the other.
commit=8ff398875c981e7cef7af15bc04cbcca96c41935 | ci=green: 1 CI run(s) for 8ff398875c981e7cef7af15bc04cbcca96c41935 all completed successfully with real steps executed.

PASS: LiveQA live test, sprint 47, round 1. Verdict: PASS.
Every LiveQA criterion was run against the published 0.2.24. The headline requirement — that the new script performs the provenance method end to end, on this very release — passed, and I proved it can fail as well as pass rather than accepting a single green run. No defects.

ENVIRONMENT
macOS 26.6.2 arm64, node v24.21.0, npm 11.19.0, git 2.55.0, Claude Code CLI 2.1.281. 2026-09-24. A clean clone at the shipped commit (the script is this repo's own dev tooling, not in package.json's `files`, same as verify-tarball.sh) and a real npx install of 0.2.24 for the shipped documentation.

REQ 1c — THE SCRIPT, RUN ON THIS RELEASE (the criterion's own words: "that is the point of Req 1c")
  bash scripts/verify-release-content.sh fully-completely 0.2.24 8ff398875c981e7cef7af15bc04cbcca96c41935
Output, verbatim in substance:
  gitHead (corroboration only -- Req 1a: reported, never decides pass/fail on its own): present and matches 8ff398875c981e7cef7af15bc04cbcca96c41935
  tarball SHA-1 recomputed independently of npm's own check: matches ba12b6ba29460ee3a32b42e3a22f6c7c855e4334
  MATCHED: 59   MISMATCHED: 0   NOT-IN-COMMIT: 0
  RELEASE CONTENT VERIFICATION PASSED
  exit 0
The three counts are reported as the requirement asks, and gitHead is labelled corroboration in the script's own output rather than by convention.

I DID NOT ACCEPT ONE GREEN RUN AS EVIDENCE THE SCRIPT WORKS
A verifier that only ever passes proves nothing, so I ran the cases that must fail and the case the sprint exists because of:
- Same release, WRONG commit (0.2.24 against 4602108, the previous release's commit): exit 1, with real per-file mismatches listed (CHANGELOG.md, .claude/agents/master-controller.md, .claude/agents/liveqa.md, package.json, scripts/mc-commit.js, scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py). So the comparison is real, not a rubber stamp.
- 0.2.22 — the release sprint 46 published with NO gitHead — against its audited commit 86c4ad5: exit 0, content PASSED (59/0/0), with gitHead reported "ABSENT -- the registry has no gitHead recorded for this version (this is exactly sprint 46's own 0.2.22 failure mode -- not a reason to fail this script, but reported plainly)". That is Req 1a's asymmetry demonstrated on the real artifact that motivated it, not asserted.
- Nonexistent version (9.9.9): exit 1, failing cleanly at the download rather than passing vacuously.

REQ 1a/1b — THE TWO CHECKS, AND WHAT EACH ANSWERS
gitHead for 0.2.24 is present and equals last_shipped_commit (8ff3988…). Content comparison independently proves the tarball is that commit's files. I report them as answering different questions, which is what the criterion asks: gitHead attests what git said at one instant and cannot detect content drift; content comparison proves what the tarball actually is and cannot detect a release published from the wrong commit whose content happens to match. The installed liveqa.md states exactly this at lines 90-91 ("Neither check replaces the other (Req 1b) — they answer different questions").
Req 1a's other half — that Pipeman's publish-time stop condition is unchanged — holds by diff: git diff 4602108..8ff3988 over .claude/agents/pipeman.md is ZERO lines. Nothing about Pipeman's own gitHead check was weakened to accommodate LiveQA's demotion of it.

REQ 1 — THE METHOD IS NOW STANDING, NOT PER-SPRINT
Installed liveqa.md carries it as its own Provenance section ("Content comparison, not `gitHead`, is the standing proof that a published release contains what was audited"), cites sprint 13's unimplemented recommendation as its origin, and names the script at line 60 with its invocation. That is the improvisation-to-documented-path change the sprint set out to make; I have improvised this same comparison in every round since sprint 35, and this round I ran the shipped script instead.

REQ 2 — THE THREE POINTERS, READ AS A USER MEETS THEM
Not read from source, but triggered live in a 0.2.24 install with HEAD detached:
- gate-commit.js and mc-commit.js both refuse with: "ERROR: HEAD is detached, currently at f0c58dd -- refusing to commit. Nothing has been committed. A publish may be in progress in this checkout (see CLAUDE.md's publish-isolation rule: Pipeman publishes from a throwaway clone, never from this checkout) -- wait for HEAD to return to a branch, then retry."
- sprint_lifecycle.py's warning names the same rule the same way.
2a is satisfied: the reference is by what the rule IS, not by sprint number, and CLAUDE.md contains that name.
2b, my own independent sweep rather than trusting the reported coverage: grep across scripts/ and .claude/ for a message naming a CLAUDE.md rule by sprint number returns one hit, mc-commit.js:90, "CLAUDE.md's own real content, sprint 36 established". That is a citation of what sprint 36 measured, not a signpost to a renamed rule, and it is still true — correctly left alone rather than swept up. The only surviving occurrence of the old "worktree-publish rule, sprint 46" string in the install is inside smoke_test.sh, where it is the regression test that fails if the stale pointer ever returns.

REQ 3 — THE PLANNING STEP
Installed master-controller.md names the four places to search before calling something unverified, including the one nothing else in this framework mentions: "sprint files, including CLOSED ones (`docs/sprints/3-done/`, `4-blocked/`, `5-abandoned/`) — a finding doesn't stop existing when its sprint closes", through to annotated tags. And it states the cost concretely rather than as principle: "Writing 'unverified' instead of looking cost a real release (0.2.22, published with no `gitHead` at all), a LiveQA FAIL round, and a full fix round, all to re-arrive at a fact already on record." Req 3b holds — nothing gained a gate; this is planning discipline and the diff shows no command refusing anything new.

ONE OBSERVATION, NOT A DEFECT
The script lives in the repository, not in an install (package.json's `files` excludes it, exactly as it excludes verify-tarball.sh and the findings docs). That is consistent and deliberate — it verifies THIS package's own releases — but it means a downstream LiveQA verifying its own project's release has the documented method in liveqa.md and no runnable tool, which is the state this sprint just fixed for us. Worth a thought if downstream installs ever need the same proof; not a sprint 47 requirement, and not something I would change without asking.
